nodes.label: Surface Allocation

nodes.label: Customer-Variable Page Count
nodes.description: First product type where surface count is customer state. Template declares pageCount: {min, max, step, default}; customer types a count, inner pages auto-populate from the single inner-page template. Steps in multiples of 4 (signature folding).

nodes.label: Gutter / Spine Margin
nodes.description: book.gutterMm — inner margin auto-mirrored by page parity (odd pages bind left, even bind right). Shift is half the gutter figure applied uniformly across a page's frames/overlays, capped by tightest element's headroom.

nodes.label: Spine Width Formula
nodes.description: spineWidthMm = (pageCount/2 leaves) × paperThicknessMm — computed dimension recomputed whenever customer changes page count. Implementation differs from PRD sketch (which double-counted) — needs Catalog Ops sign-off.

nodes.label: pagesToSpreads

nodes.label: EXPORT_RETENTION_DAYS

nodes.label: graphify knowledge graph workflow
nodes.rationale: Use `graphify update .` (AST-only, no LLM key) not `graphify . --update` which aborts without GEMINI/ANTHROPIC key. Read node counts from GRAPH_REPORT.md, not CLAUDE.md — the stated counts drifted.

nodes.label: Git and shipping hard constraints
nodes.rationale: main is production (deploy.sh pulls main). Branch from freshly-pulled main before any edit; never push/PR/merge without explicit go-ahead; never git add -A (shared checkout); delete remote branch after merge; never predict PR numbers. Autonomous implement→merge chains left the user reviewing merges instead of deciding them (PRs #41–#53).

nodes.label: No direct DOM manipulation rule
nodes.rationale: React owns the DOM; mutating nodes underneath desyncs the virtual DOM and innerHTML is an XSS sink. Exempt: offscreen canvases, Fabric/Three roots via useRef, transient download anchors, window listeners in effects.

nodes.label: Backend standalone test modules
nodes.rationale: No pytest / manage.py test; every services/tests/test_*.py has a __main__ runner. CI globs them so the count is pinned nowhere. Run via container with --entrypoint override because entrypoint.sh ignores $@ and would boot gunicorn. Backend image bakes source in via COPY — rebuild before testing or you test the last build.

nodes.label: Frontend Jest + happy-dom harness
nodes.rationale: happy-dom instead of jsdom because jsdom auto-requires the native canvas module Fabric.js peer-deps.

nodes.label: Browser verification via embed token / minted NextAuth cookie
nodes.rationale: Editor route is not auth-gated so an embed session token opens it; auth-gated pages need a NextAuth JWT minted with the frontend AUTH_SECRET (differs from root .env).
nodes.norm_label: browser verification via embed token / minted nextauth cookie

nodes.label: NextAuth cookie becomes HttpOnly after first session call
nodes.rationale: A second document.cookie write of authjs.session-token is silently ignored once /api/auth/session re-issues it HttpOnly; sign out server-side via /api/auth/signout first. Cookie absent from document.cookie does not mean no session — read /api/auth/session.
nodes.norm_label: nextauth cookie becomes httponly after first session call

nodes.label: Layout-card action buttons ignore synthetic clicks
nodes.rationale: Automation artifact reproduced on unmodified main, not a bug; verify via code + curl and one manual click.
nodes.norm_label: layout-card action buttons ignore synthetic clicks

nodes.label: Unified server-side render pipeline
nodes.rationale: The client-side '≤20 canvases render in browser' shortcut was removed in v1.8 so every Submit/Download goes through one Celery contract that handles webhooks, large batches and resumable uploads identically. Trade-off: small jobs pay ~10–20 s extra upload+poll latency.

nodes.label: Access-mode invariant (dashboard == embed output)
nodes.rationale: Dashboard login flow and iframe embed flow must produce the same print output for identical inputs; only auth and delivery differ.

nodes.label: Chunked upload API
nodes.rationale: 2 MB chunks, 4 files parallel; UUID v4 regex guard on chunk/complete views prevents path traversal; 50 MB per-file limit; staged under UPLOADS_DIR/.chunks/{upload_id}/.

nodes.label: POST /api/editor/render contract
nodes.rationale: Per-frame {upload_id, offset_x, offset_y, scale, rotation, fit_mode}; order_id resolution: X-Order-ID header beats body; 202 with job_id + status_url.

nodes.label: Direct partner API (/api/layout/generate)
nodes.rationale: Always async, poll render-status; soft_proof/tiff_cmyk/callback_url body params removed v1.8; does NOT support books (never builds canvases_meta so would flood every page with the whole photo list).

nodes.label: API surface separation cleanup target
nodes.rationale: Remove the unreachable synchronous helper in GenerateLayoutView and route direct-partner + editor/embed submissions through one shared render-submission service; CanvasData upsert / RenderJob creation / queue selection are duplicated across the two views. Not started.

nodes.label: Embed session & order-id flow
nodes.rationale: caller → POST /api/embed/session {order_id, callback_url, qty} → token in iframe URL → proxy resolves token, caches tuple 110 min, injects X-Order-ID / X-Callback-URL / X-Include-Uploads / X-Order-Qty. order_id and callback_url never appear in the iframe URL. order_id regex ^[A-Za-z0-9_.\-]{1,64}$.

nodes.label: Embed proxy cache tuple invariant
nodes.rationale: Anything injected as a header must be in the cached tuple — a field resolved but not cached is present on the session's first request and silently absent for the remaining 110 minutes.

nodes.label: Embed proxy allowlist (path AND method)
nodes.rationale: Prefix-only until 2026-09-03 with 'GET only' as a comment. fonts/holidays/calendar-styles accept ops writes upstream and the proxy injects the session's real api_key — with an ops-flagged key (DIRECT is ops-flagged) an embed token in a customer URL could PUT holiday data. Check runs before token resolution so stolen tokens can't probe Django auth. Pinned by allowlist.test.ts.

nodes.label: Signed embed webhook delivery
nodes.rationale: Only when EmbedSession.callback_url is set; payload {order_id, job_id, status, download_url, print/mock/uploads_download_url, expires_at, file_count, layout_name, export_format}; X-Signature sha256 HMAC keyed by api_key. No internal OMS push exists.

nodes.label: One archive or three (?content=)
nodes.rationale: download_url is the combined archive (unchanged, no migration). print/mock/uploads URLs are the same job packaged one part per archive for callers storing mock and print separately (printo.in does). uploads_download_url is null when include_uploads=false. Nothing is duplicated on disk; content=mock 404s rather than returning an empty ZIP.

nodes.label: Sliding embed session TTL
nodes.rationale: 2 h expiry, extended by 1 h whenever remaining lifetime < 30 min; active editing never hits a hard cutoff, idle sessions expire on schedule.

nodes.label: iframe frame-ancestors CSP
nodes.rationale: /layout/* and /editor/layout/* allow 'self', https://printo.in, https://*.printo.in; override via NEXT_PUBLIC_EMBED_FRAME_ANCESTORS. Legacy /embed/layout/* removed because it read ?apiKey= from the URL.

nodes.label: Order quantity (qty) rule — deliberately asymmetric
nodes.rationale: Over qty: hard cap both sides (modal Keep first N / Choose again; server 400). Under qty: warn and proceed both sides. qty is caller-supplied so a wrong value must not strand a real order — a customer who can't buy costs more than one who orders 12 and submits 8. qty_violation has one '>' and no lower bound. Counts photo placements, not distinct uploads (auto-fill repeats one photo). Single-surface only; server exempts calendar/book.

nodes.label: Server qty check fails open
nodes.rationale: Unreadable layout, absent header, unparseable header all mean 'don't check'. A tamper guard that can 400 a legitimate order on its own uncertainty is worse than no guard. Server half is deliberately narrower than the browser's so it can never reject a submission the editor allowed.

nodes.label: postMessage contract (pe:render_job)
nodes.rationale: targetOrigin is locked, never '*': ancestorOrigins[0] → referrer origin → NEXT_PUBLIC_EMBED_PARENT_ORIGIN → https://printo.in. Payload includes order_id and job_id so eavesdropping must be prevented.

nodes.label: Smart downscale (2× frame target)
nodes.rationale: Pre-shrinks a 12 MP source to ~0.64 M working pixels (~95% memory reduction per frame). The defensive img.copy() was removed in v1.10 — a wasted ~50 MB memcpy per frame.

nodes.label: Engine memory hygiene
nodes.rationale: with Image.open blocks, explicit .close() + del + gc.collect() per canvas; without it 200-canvas batches accumulated several GB before worker recycle. worker_max_tasks_per_child=50 relies on this.

nodes.label: Per-frame transform order
nodes.rationale: rotate(expand) → smart downscale → extra_scale → cover/contain resize → pan offset at paste. Mirrored in dpi-utils and fabric-renderer; change one and update all.

nodes.label: Single Celery worker drains priority,standard
nodes.rationale: The second priority worker was retired with the CMYK path in v1.8 and nothing routes to priority since. The survivor listens to both because celery.py still documents apply_async(queue='priority') — an unconsumed task would sit in Redis forever with no error. Safety net, not a QoS tier: Celery round-robins across -Q queues.

nodes.label: Celery retry strategy
nodes.rationale: self.retry() exponential 2s→4s→8s, max 3; MemoryError and SoftTimeLimitExceeded skip retries; never autoretry_for. acks_late + reject_on_worker_lost requeue on worker death.

nodes.label: transaction.on_commit dispatch inside atomic()
nodes.rationale: Call on_commit inside the atomic block so the task fires only after commit; outside a transaction it executes immediately, which works but is fragile.

nodes.label: GC runs every 6 hours, not nightly
nodes.rationale: Retention 3 days + Indian business hours means exports expire in a 03:00–12:00 UTC wave. The old 02:00 sweep sat just before it and collected 2% of pending rows; effective retention was ~4 days and disk sawtoothed 82→93% while the sweep was healthy. Two wrong root causes were chased before plotting expiries by hour. Re-plot if retention or timezone changes.
nodes.norm_label: gc runs every 6 hours, not nightly

nodes.label: GC status: stale vs failing
nodes.rationale: gc_last_run.json under STORAGE_ROOT (bind-mounted, survives recreation, no migration). stale = no recent successful sweep; failing = last attempt raised with last_error. The failure record exists because staleness cannot say why and reads identically to 'never scheduled' — that ambiguity let a wrong diagnosis run two days. Not on /api/health because that drives Docker restarts. Never infer GC health from is_deleted counts (tombstones are hard-deleted in the same pass, so it reads 0 either way).

nodes.label: Celery stale DB connection hardening
nodes.rationale: CONN_MAX_AGE is enforced from request signals Celery never fires, so a worker connection can stay checked out until the socket drops. Hooks close_old_connections on task_prerun AND task_postrun, plus CONN_HEALTH_CHECKS=True. Hardening, not a fix for an observed incident.

nodes.label: Orphaned export directory sweep
nodes.rationale: Formed because async-render cleanup filtered on status='completed', so jobs killed mid-render kept files after the CanvasData cascade removed the RenderJob. GC_ORPHAN_SWEEP defaults to dry_run because this is the one sweep that deletes on the absence of evidence. Five conditions must all hold (UUID name, no RenderJob, no ExportedResult path, no CanvasData.order_id match, mtime older than retention+1 day). A DB failure keeps everything.

nodes.label: Abandoned chunk-upload staging sweep
nodes.rationale: Deletes by default (unlike orphan_exports) because .part fragments are unusable without the /complete call. Uses the newest mtime of the directory and its contents so a slow live upload is never a candidate. Briefly duplicated an inline block in garbage_collector_task under a different counter name — grep the whole task before adding a sweep.

nodes.label: Layouts moved from disk to Postgres LayoutCatalogue (PR #111)
nodes.rationale: Git-tracked layouts rewritten at runtime by the ops UI made prod diverge (20 deleted, 11 renamed) and broke git pull. Postgres gives audit trail, soft delete, pg_dump coverage and decouples identity from the OS filesystem. Migration 0016 created schema + idempotent import; 0017 imported 14 prod layouts on 2026-09-04. Note: the later 'Storage Files' section of CLAUDE.md still says 'Layouts are not in Postgres' — that paragraph is stale relative to this one.
nodes.norm_label: layouts moved from disk to postgres layoutcatalogue (pr #111)

nodes.label: LayoutEngine must receive layout_definition
nodes.rationale: Missing layout_definition causes [Errno 2] No such file or directory on render. Four call sites were found not passing it during the 2026-09-04 audit. Any code instantiating LayoutEngine must query LayoutCatalogue first.

nodes.label: Layout identity = LayoutCatalogue.name (case-sensitive)
nodes.rationale: When layouts were files a name/filename case mismatch worked on Mac but 404'd on Linux prod. Queries use the name column, never the definition's internal field.

nodes.label: Scalar API reference (/docs/api/) from drf-spectacular
nodes.rationale: A view without @extend_schema is dropped, not merely undocumented; SECURITY_DEFINITIONS is a drf-yasg name silently ignored — auth schemes live in api/schema.py as OpenApiAuthenticationExtension subclasses. Views with AllowAny + in-handler ops gating need explicit per-operation auth=. Validate with spectacular --validate --fail-on-warn.

nodes.label: HEIC decoding chain (three decoders)
nodes.rationale: heic2any (2021 libheif) → browser createImageBitmap (Safari only) → POST /api/heic/convert (pillow-heif). iOS 18 writes tmap gain-map HEIC that heic2any cannot read and Chrome/Firefox have no HEIC codec, so a modern iPhone photo is undecodable in Chrome without the server. Server keeps the ICC profile (colour-managed later) and writes no EXIF (libheif already applied irot/imir). Does not register_heif_opener globally.

nodes.label: Auto-orientation: MediaPipe Pose + aspect heuristic
nodes.rationale: Server BlazePose nose-to-shoulder vector snapped to cardinal with 30° dead-zone catches subjects stored sideways; aspect heuristic is the fallback. Inline rather than Celery because generateCanvases needs the rotation before drawing the preview. Client memoises per file.

nodes.label: AUTO_ORIENTATION_MODE (mediapipe/hybrid/off)
nodes.rationale: Lite ~5 MB for ≤2 cores, Full ~9 MB for ≥4 cores; /api/config exposes the mode so the client skips detect when off. Needs libgl1 + libglib2.0-0 or import silently disables the service.

nodes.label: Three-tier role model (Admin/Ops/Editor)
nodes.rationale: is_staff = Admin (django-admin), is_ops_team = Ops (template/calendar/holiday writes), authenticated = Editor. Rules in lib/roles.ts so a button cannot appear for someone a gate denies. Reverses PR #24 which opened template management to any authenticated user. Reads stay open (GET ops/layouts lists templates).

nodes.label: Ops privilege gate must live in the internal proxy
nodes.rationale: Everything through the internal proxy presents the shared ops-flagged INTERNAL_API_KEY, so Django's IsOpsTeam sees one privileged identity regardless of who is signed in. Only the proxy knows the human. A Django-side permission class cannot substitute — the trap PR #24 fell into.
nodes.norm_label: ops privilege gate must live in the internal proxy

nodes.label: Deactivated employees rejected per request
nodes.rationale: PIA does not refuse login for deactivated employees and a session minted earlier stays valid, so isRegistrationActive is re-checked in the internal proxy and verify-django-admin. Absent status counts as active on purpose — failing closed would lock everyone out if PIA dropped the field.

nodes.label: Django admin SSO via signed identity headers
nodes.rationale: Prod had zero auth_user rows so the admin was unreachable. verify-django-admin returns X-PE-Admin-Id/-Email/-Exp/-Sig; nginx auth_request_set forwards them; DjangoAdminSSOMiddleware verifies and provisions a passwordless superuser. Signature is HMAC keyed by HMAC(EMBED_INTERNAL_SECRET, 'django-admin-sso/v1') (purpose-bound so it can't replay into the embed-token path) with 60 s TTL, because anything reaching backend:8000 on the Docker network could otherwise mint superuser headers. Flags asserted every request; ProxyAuthenticationMiddleware guarded /admin/ while the admin was at /django-admin/ so it had never run.
nodes.norm_label: django admin sso via signed identity headers

nodes.label: PIA flags captured only at sign-in
nodes.rationale: jwt callback sets flags inside if (user); refresh returns the existing token. A flag granted in PIA after last login needs sign-out/in. [pia-login] log prints every flag with its type.
nodes.norm_label: pia flags captured only at sign-in

nodes.label: NextAuth v5 Credentials login against PIA
nodes.rationale: JWT strategy; authorize separates bad credentials (4xx → null) from outage (5xx → PiaServiceUnavailableError, timeout → PiaTimeoutError) so users don't retype passwords during a PIA incident. AbortSignal.timeout(10s).
nodes.norm_label: nextauth v5 credentials login against pia

nodes.label: Google Sign-In via PIA (/auth/google/login/)
nodes.rationale: GIS button returns an ID token; provider posts it to PIA which returns the same token payload as /auth/, so jwt/session/refresh are identical. @printo.in domain gate enforced server-side after PIA validates (hd claim or verified email). Client id public; no client secret.

nodes.label: Open-redirect clamp in redirect callback
nodes.rationale: Relative paths join baseUrl; absolute URLs only same-origin; malformed → baseUrl.

nodes.label: Per-IP login rate limit (5/60s, in-memory)
nodes.rationale: Single-process Map; swap to Redis if the frontend container is scaled horizontally. IP from nginx X-Real-IP / right-most XFF hop, never the spoofable left-most.

nodes.label: Augmented NextAuth Session shape
nodes.rationale: user.role is legacy and expresses none of the tiers; is_staff/is_ops_team/registration_status read through lib/roles.ts; is_super_user never existed in PIA and is_superuser is disputed — never gate on it. session.error === 'RefreshAccessTokenError' is checked in proxy.ts, internal proxy and every protected page.

nodes.label: Three frame renderers — the drift trap
nodes.rationale: Live editor (FabricEditor.tsx), thumbnail (fabric-renderer.ts) and print (engine.py) are independent implementations; add to one and it silently disagrees with the other two. frame-fill.ts unifies the two client renderers (the blur once appeared in thumbnail and print but not the live editor).
nodes.norm_label: three frame renderers — the drift trap

nodes.label: TS↔Python parity test pattern
nodes.rationale: Maths deliberately duplicated across the language boundary is pinned by parity suites on both sides: caption-layout ↔ _resolve_caption_box, calendar.ts ↔ calendar_renderer.py, checkOrderQty ↔ order_qty.py (asymmetric on purpose), book-layout.ts ↔ book_layout.py.

nodes.label: Tailwind `indigo` scale overridden with Printo purple
nodes.rationale: indigo-600 = #64318E so every existing call site was re-skinned at once instead of touching hundreds; class names lie about colour. Don't fix a class back to hex or add a second purple scale. Accent orange #F17A26 has no scale.
nodes.norm_label: tailwind `indigo` scale overridden with printo purple

nodes.label: isExport flag hides outlines/overlays in output
nodes.norm_label: isexport flag hides outlines/overlays in output

nodes.label: Ops-config storage files are git-tracked AND runtime-written
nodes.rationale: fonts.json, holidays/, calendar_styles/ (and formerly layouts/, masks/) are committed and rewritten by the ops UI, so git pull on prod fails when a commit touches a changed file. Never git reset --hard or checkout -- storage/ on prod — it resurrects obsolete layouts alongside live ones. Resolve by checking out one named file.
nodes.norm_label: ops-config storage files are git-tracked and runtime-written

nodes.label: SKU→layout mapping removed (2026-09-04)
nodes.rationale: printo.in resolves SKU to layout on its side and passes the resolved name into the embed session; a second mapping here was one more place to drift and never carried real data. Both smoke tests assert /api/sku-layouts/ returns 404.

nodes.label: Calendar product type (v1.13)
nodes.rationale: Regular multi-surface layout plus productType 'calendar' and monthRange + calendars[] + calendar style block; ops UI at /editor/layouts/calendar/[name].

nodes.label: Calendar render path
nodes.rationale: materialize_surfaces expands one template into 12 per-month surfaces; poster aggregation merges them into one page when monthRange.count == 1; filenames from displayLabel ('January 2026.png'); partial failure cleans up all outputs and raises a tagged RuntimeError naming the surface.

nodes.label: Calendar per-day entries keyed by ISO date
nodes.rationale: One flat product-wide {iso_date: [CellOverride]} map anchored to globally-unique dates, not tile positions, so photo-canvas count and English↔Financial flips can never lose or misplace entries. Legacy 12-slot cellsPerCanvas still read.
nodes.norm_label: calendar per-day entries keyed by iso date

nodes.label: Calendar photo→month mapping (i mod N)
nodes.rationale: Frontend caps photo canvases at 12; engine renders exactly 12 outputs, month i uses photo-canvas (i mod N). Previously N photos produced 12·N files.

nodes.label: Calendar customer-facing fail-safes (PRD §11)
nodes.rationale: Feb 29 toast, image-expired re-upload prompt, calendar-type flip orphan warning, partial render-failure cleanup.

nodes.label: Book / photobook product type (backend only)
nodes.rationale: Mirrors the calendar materialize architecture, not its renderer — a book page is just frames. Ops author writes cover + innerPage (+ optional backCover), each with its own canvas so a hardcover wrap can be larger than the block. No ops UI, customer editor, or smoke test yet.

nodes.label: Book page count is customer state
nodes.rationale: book.pageCount {min,max,step,default}; resolve_page_count snaps UP to the step grid so the customer never silently loses a page. Covers addressed by role, never index, so count changes can't renumber them.
nodes.norm_label: book page count is customer state

nodes.label: Book gutter mirroring by page parity (D5)
nodes.rationale: One gutterMm mirrored: odd pages bind left, even bind right; shift gutterMm/2 applied uniformly and capped by the element with least headroom so collage elements move together. Covers never shifted.
nodes.norm_label: book gutter mirroring by page parity (d5)

nodes.label: Spine width formula (leaves, not sides)
nodes.rationale: (pageCount/2) × paperThicknessMm + 2 × coverThicknessMm — differs from the PRD sketch which double-counts. Which convention Catalog Ops means by 'paper thickness' is unconfirmed; sign off against a printed sample before any cover ships.

nodes.label: Book filenames as zero-padded collation order
nodes.rationale: '01 Front Cover', '02 Page 01' … so an alphabetical ZIP listing is already print order; one ZIP, no separate cover archive.
nodes.norm_label: book filenames as zero-padded collation order

nodes.label: R1: customer-variable surface count is an open frontend problem
nodes.rationale: Books are the first product where surface count is chosen by the customer; normalizeLayout, SurfaceState, autosave/restore and canvas-merge identity reuse are untouched — the hard part of Phase 5/6.
nodes.norm_label: r1: customer-variable surface count is an open frontend problem

nodes.label: Minimal cache-first Service Worker
nodes.rationale: Cache-first only for content-hashed /_next/static/* and /static/*; never HTML, API or auth-gated; production-only registration so dev changes always hit the network; bump CACHE_VERSION to bust.

nodes.label: Never-lose-edits: reuse canvases by file identity
nodes.rationale: canvas-merge.ts plans reuse by name:size:lastModified not grid position, so re-pick/add/remove/reorder keeps pans/zooms/overlays on the right page. 'Add Files' must append — a native file input pick is never cumulative; feeding the raw pick into setFiles wiped earlier canvases until PR #24.
nodes.norm_label: never-lose-edits: reuse canvases by file identity

nodes.label: IndexedDB File persistence (B1) with in-memory degrade
nodes.rationale: Files keyed by (orderId, fileId) so refresh restores originals and blob URLs; falls back to an in-memory map when IndexedDB is blocked (Safari ITP in a cross-site iframe); prunes other orders on quota; FrameState carries fileName/fileSize so the lost-photo guard fires even when persistence failed.
nodes.norm_label: indexeddb file persistence (b1) with in-memory degrade

nodes.label: Upload resume via acked-chunk WeakMap
nodes.rationale: Failed submit re-sends only failed files, skipping acked chunks; byte-weighted progress; a GC'd session (404) restarts once.

nodes.label: Per-surface render grouping (canvases_meta)
nodes.rationale: Each canvas carries surface_key so the engine slices photos/transforms/overlays per surface and an omitted side prints blank rather than the other side's photo. Frontend must send the REAL surface key even for one surface — a literal 'canvas' matched nothing and printed blank. Gated on canvases_meta so direct partner callers are byte-identical.

nodes.label: Submit guards: warn and proceed
nodes.rationale: Empty-surface and duplicate-fill warnings never block; qty auto-fill fingerprints are exempt via intentionalDupesRef.

nodes.label: SSRF protection for callback URLs
nodes.rationale: validate_public_https_url at session-create rejects private/reserved/loopback/link-local/metadata; post_webhook_safely pins the socket to the validated IP under a lock so DNS can't rebind, allow_redirects=False. Never requests.post a customer callback_url directly.

nodes.label: Trusted client IP: X-Real-IP / right-most XFF hop
nodes.rationale: Shared module-level _get_client_ip so a spoofed XFF can never be trusted by the rate limiter and rejected by the audit trail (or vice versa).
nodes.norm_label: trusted client ip: x-real-ip / right-most xff hop

nodes.label: Redis split: durable broker vs disposable cache
nodes.rationale: Broker is noeviction + appendonly so cached values can never evict queued render messages and in-flight jobs survive restart; cache is allkeys-lru with no volume. Settings derives REDIS_CACHE_URL by swapping /0 → /1 unless overridden.
nodes.norm_label: redis split: durable broker vs disposable cache

nodes.label: render_canvas_task poison-pill guard
nodes.rationale: Counts only genuine broker redeliveries via delivery_info.redelivered, aborts after 3 crash-redeliveries (not self.retry re-runs); 500 MB disk-full pre-flight.

nodes.label: DPDP order data purge
nodes.rationale: DELETE /api/ops/orders/<order_id>/purge, ops-only, not on the embed allowlist; hard-deletes uploads/exports/CanvasData/EmbedSession rows and files; cross-tenant requires explicit all_tenants=true; keeps upload files shared with a surviving order. UploadedFile.order_id (0011) exists because autosave blanked CanvasData.image_paths so purge reported files_deleted: 0.

nodes.label: Backups (pg_dump + ops-config tar), cron 03:15 UTC
nodes.rationale: Scheduled on prod since 2026-08-28 — CLAUDE.md claimed 'not scheduled' until 2026-09-04. The cron comment's '02:00 GC' justification is stale (GC is every 6 h) but 03:15 still falls between sweeps.

nodes.label: CI workflow (backend loop + frontend typecheck/lint/jest)
nodes.rationale: Org is on GitHub Free with Actions billing-locked so checks may show red unrelated to code — verify locally.

nodes.label: Deploy fail-fast on required secrets
nodes.rationale: Compose aborts on missing AUTH_SECRET; Django won't boot with the default DJANGO_SECRET_KEY under DEBUG=0; internal proxy 500s without INTERNAL_API_KEY; internal ports bind 127.0.0.1 only; NEXT_PUBLIC_DIRECT_API_KEY build-arg removed.

nodes.label: editor_state vs render_state ownership contract (0008)
nodes.rationale: editor_state is frontend-owned (autosave via CanvasStateView); render_state is pipeline-owned (EditorRenderView at submit, read by render_canvas_task). Separating the two writers means submit no longer wipes the autosaved design and a post-submit autosave can't strip a queued job's payload. Never cross the streams.

nodes.label: API audit trail (APIRequest, 0014)
nodes.rationale: The model existed from the initial commit with nothing writing to it, so count()==0 read as proof a leaked key was never used. SET_NULL keeps history across key rotation; auth_source denormalises the actor. The write can never break a request. error_message is NULL for framework-level rejections (RequestDataTooBig) — request_size_bytes is what made the autosave-400 diagnosis possible.

nodes.label: AUDIT_EXEMPT_PREFIXES (health, config, render-status, chunk PUTs)
nodes.rationale: render-status alone produced ~1,500 rows/hour during one job. Adding a customer-data endpoint that matches an exemption creates a silent blind spot; test_audit_middleware.py pins both directions.

nodes.label: deploy.sh (runs on prod, pulls main, migrates before swap)
nodes.rationale: Push to main before deploying. Prod .env differs from local — edit in place, never scp over it. A deploy.sh change only takes effect on the deploy after the one that pulls it.
nodes.norm_label: deploy.sh (runs on prod, pulls main, migrates before swap)

nodes.label: nginx.conf single-file bind mount binds the inode
nodes.rationale: git pull replaces the file, so a running proxy keeps the config it booted with and nginx -s reload re-reads the same stale inode. deploy.sh sync_proxy_config compares container copy vs disk and recreates only when they differ. On 2026-09-04 admin-SSO headers were 'deployed' while the proxy still ran an August config.
nodes.norm_label: nginx.conf single-file bind mount binds the inode

nodes.label: entrypoint.sh web path ignores $@
nodes.rationale: Always migrate → seed API keys → exec gunicorn, so docker-compose run backend <cmd> hangs forever; use --entrypoint to bypass. Worker/beat paths honour $1. Backend self-migrates on every boot.

nodes.label: collectstatic build-time inline DJANGO_SECRET_KEY
nodes.rationale: collectstatic runs at image build before any .env exists; the DEBUG=0 secret-key guard would abort the build, so the Dockerfile supplies an inline build-only key never baked into ENV. Verify Dockerfile/settings changes with a CLEAN build — a cached layer hides the failure.

nodes.label: Observability owned outside this repo
nodes.rationale: Loki/Promtail/Grafana/Alloy removed 2026-09-07 — the server lead maintains monitoring, and two half-owned stacks is worse than one. Point the external collector at container stdout (json-file 50 MB × 3). Worker logs are lost on every --force-recreate, so capture them before redeploying.

nodes.label: Two server-side proxy routes (internal vs embed)
nodes.rationale: The browser never sees an API key: /api/internal/proxy uses the NextAuth cookie + INTERNAL_API_KEY; /api/embed/proxy uses X-Embed-Token. src/proxy.ts is unrelated despite the name — it is the Next.js 16 middleware successor.
nodes.norm_label: two server-side proxy routes (internal vs embed)

nodes.label: P1: 37% of canvas autosaves rejected with 400
nodes.rationale: editor_state embeds base64 data: previews (~350 kB × 15–32/order) so 1,569 autosaves averaging 16 MB (peak 93 MB) hit DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE=10 MB; ~25 GB uploaded and discarded in 27 days. Invisible because renders use render_state and same-browser refresh recovers from IndexedDB. Do NOT raise the limit (gunicorn buffers bodies per request on a 2-core box) — strip regenerable previews; success signal is the 400 rate reaching zero.
nodes.norm_label: p1: 37% of canvas autosaves rejected with 400

nodes.label: image_loader: single choke point for customer photos
nodes.rationale: open_source_rgba applies EXIF orientation and ICC→sRGB via lcms2 (Display-P3 iPhone, AdobeRGB, CMYK-tagged), fail-open on malformed profiles; outputs tagged sRGB. Image.open().convert('RGBA') directly discards the profile and shifts colours in print.
nodes.norm_label: image_loader: single choke point for customer photos

nodes.label: Single bundled font: Inter Variable
nodes.rationale: No font picker (PRD §11.7); variable axis serves any weight from one 859 KB ttf; falls back to PIL default with a one-time log; startup_check warns if absent.

nodes.label: Migration 0012: one retention clock via stored expires_at
nodes.rationale: GC swept uploads/exports on created_at + retention recomputed at sweep time, so lowering EXPORT_RETENTION_DAYS acted retroactively — deleting files whose expiry had already been sent to a partner as webhook expires_at, silently yielding ZIPs without 1_customer_uploads/. Backfill reads the retention in force at migration time — deploy before lowering the env var.
nodes.norm_label: migration 0012: one retention clock via stored expires_at

nodes.label: Migration 0013: image_paths default=list
nodes.rationale: CanvasStateView.put keeps image_paths out of update_or_create defaults (writing [] every 2 s caused the erasure bug), but the NOT NULL column had no default so the first autosave for any new order 500'd and no row was ever created. A model default applies on INSERT only.

nodes.label: Iframe adopts the EmbedSession order id
nodes.rationale: EditorInitView echoes X-Order-ID as order_id; page sets it before setLayout; CanvasStateView.put prefers the header over the path param while get keeps the path for legacy restore.
nodes.norm_label: iframe adopts the embedsession order id

nodes.label: Mobile: pinch-to-zoom + tap-to-swap
nodes.rationale: Fabric discards the second touch so pinch-utils feeds FrameState directly; touch has no HTML5 drag so swapCards/tap-to-swap replaces it; customer base is mostly phone/tablet.

nodes.label: Modal accessibility (Escape, focus trap, dialog semantics)
nodes.norm_label: modal accessibility (escape, focus trap, dialog semantics)

nodes.label: Environment-driven runtime configuration
nodes.rationale: No per-environment config files; DEBUG defaults off; MAX_UPLOAD_FILE_SIZE_MB is the single source; GC_STALE_AFTER_HOURS=36 so a merely-late run doesn't cry wolf; API_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS=90 outlives the data it describes.

nodes.label: Security rules summary
nodes.rationale: API keys never in URLs; UUID v4 validation before opening request-derived paths; IsAuthenticatedWithAPIKey on new endpoints; embed allowlist-only; postMessage targetOrigin never '*'; order_id regex not to be relaxed (flows into headers, logs, paths).

nodes.label: MAX_IMAGE_DIMENSION_PX decompression-bomb guard
nodes.rationale: Raised 8192→16384 so 48–65 MP photos upload; engine caps total pixels separately at 500 MP and smart-downscales.

nodes.label: Effective print-DPI low-res warning
nodes.rationale: dpi-utils mirrors the placement math exactly; DPI_WARN=150 / DPI_CRITICAL=100 strict <; non-blocking pills and notices.

nodes.label: README technology stack
nodes.rationale: Django 5.0.6 + DRF, Postgres 16 tuned (shared_buffers 128MB, work_mem 8MB), Celery 5 + Redis 7 split broker/cache, Gunicorn gthread (2×nproc+1), Next.js 16 standalone, React 19, Fabric.js 7.2 lazy-loaded, nginx 1.27 with Cloudflare Origin Certificate.

nodes.label: README services table
nodes.rationale: Still says celery-beat runs 'daily GC at 02:00 UTC' — CLAUDE.md says the GC moved to every 6 hours. Stale claim.

nodes.label: README quick start / first-run cert bootstrap
nodes.rationale: Fresh clone crash-loops proxy until a self-signed origin cert exists; .env.local overrides compose env; INTERNAL_API_URL must be http://backend:8000/api inside Docker.
nodes.norm_label: readme quick start / first-run cert bootstrap

nodes.label: README direct partner generation (curl example)
nodes.rationale: Always async, order_id mandatory; 202 with job_id/status_url/queue/estimated_wait_seconds; poll then download.

nodes.label: README webhook delivery section
nodes.rationale: Documents an 8-field payload without the print/mock/uploads_download_url trio that CLAUDE.md and INTEGRATION.md describe — README is behind on the content split.

nodes.label: README async queue architecture diagram
nodes.rationale: At-least-once delivery, 3× backoff retries in RenderJob.retry_count, on_commit Redis failure marks job failed, webhook task retries 5× and sets requires_manual_review on final failure.

nodes.label: README security section + production checklist
nodes.rationale: Says INTERNAL_API_KEY must equal DIRECT_API_KEY in several places; CLAUDE.md says they are independent as of feat/independent-internal-api-key (a shared value only logs a warning and skips the INTERNAL seed). Stale in README.

nodes.label: README file storage tree
nodes.rationale: Still lists storage/layouts/ and storage/masks/ as on-disk directories although layouts moved to Postgres on 2026-09-04.

nodes.label: README environment variables reference
nodes.rationale: Follows .env.example as source of truth; includes EXPORT_RETENTION_DAYS_UNDER_PRESSURE and GUNICORN_* tunables not listed in CLAUDE.md.

nodes.label: README troubleshooting table
nodes.rationale: Jobs stuck in queued → check workers/Redis; ClientFetchError → INTERNAL_API_URL; dashboard 500 → INTERNAL_API_KEY missing; webhook failures → requires_manual_review after 5 failures.

nodes.label: README migrations table (latest 0014)
nodes.rationale: Lists migrations through 0014 only; CLAUDE.md lists 0015_embedsession_qty and the LayoutCatalogue section names 0016/0017. README is two to three migrations behind.

nodes.label: README production deployment steps
nodes.rationale: Docker install, .env required values, Cloudflare Origin Certificate paste, docker-compose up, scale workers for festival seasons.

nodes.label: README: two server-side proxies, no key in browser
nodes.norm_label: readme: two server-side proxies, no key in browser

nodes.label: Storage migration: executive summary
nodes.rationale: Six phases moved layouts from git-tracked JSON to Postgres LayoutCatalogue with S3 support for masks/calendar assets; zero breaking changes to customer APIs or print output. Branch feat/storage-migration-layouts-to-postgres-s3, 8 commits, 2026-09-04.

nodes.label: Phase 1: LayoutCatalogue model + migration 0016 + export script
nodes.rationale: Case-sensitive unique name, JSONField definition, audit fields, is_deprecated soft delete, product_type inference, composite indexes, CheckConstraint on imported_at/imported_by. Migration 0016 is idempotent with an intentional NOP reverse.
nodes.norm_label: phase 1: layoutcatalogue model + migration 0016 + export script

nodes.label: Phase 2: S3Storage + get_storage factory
nodes.rationale: S3Storage fail-fast on missing AWS creds; list_layouts queries LayoutCatalogue (no S3 LIST); multipart assemble_chunks with cleanup on failure; key prefixes uploads/{order_id}/, masks/, exports/, ops-config/.

nodes.label: Phase 3: views query LayoutCatalogue
nodes.rationale: ListLayoutsView, GetLayoutView, EditorInitView, LayoutManagementView, ExternalLayoutDetailView switched from filesystem to ORM; cache keys/TTL/response schema unchanged; EditorInitView reuses GetLayoutView cache keys.

nodes.label: Atomic layout cache invalidation
nodes.rationale: invalidate_layout_caches deletes layouts_list_all + ops_layouts_list_all + layout_detail:{name}:* together, wrapped so it never fails the API; on rename clears both names. Prevents silent wrong-print bugs from a stale cached layout.

nodes.label: Phase 4: MaskDownloadView presigned URLs + mask upload
nodes.rationale: S3: presigned URL (1 h) + 301; local: FileResponse; path traversal guard; mask embedded as layout['maskUrl'].
nodes.norm_label: phase 4: maskdownloadview presigned urls + mask upload

nodes.label: Mask key migration on layout rename
nodes.rationale: copy_object then delete_file; non-fatal on failure (logs warning, still HTTP 200); tries common extensions until the mask is found.
nodes.norm_label: mask key migration on layout rename

nodes.label: Phase 5: services/asset_store.py S3-first with local fallback
nodes.rationale: read_asset(asset_type, asset_name) for calendar_styles/holidays/palettes/fonts; tries S3 ops-config/ then local; AssetNotFoundError only when both fail; readers keep a 5-min Redis cache.
nodes.norm_label: phase 5: services/asset_store.py s3-first with local fallback

nodes.label: Phase 6: tests + deployment runbook
nodes.rationale: api/tests/test_layout_catalogue.py and test_cache_invalidation.py; runbook with 7 success criteria and ~1 h timeline.

nodes.label: Render data flow after migration
nodes.rationale: EditorRenderView queries LayoutCatalogue by name, snapshots definition, dispatches render_canvas_task; engine loads layout from DB snapshot not disk.

nodes.label: Known limitations / future work
nodes.rationale: S3 untested in prod (run STORAGE_BACKEND=local); calendar asset writes still go to disk; GenerateLayoutView still read layouts from disk at time of writing (CLAUDE.md later records this as fixed in the 2026-09-04 audit).

nodes.label: Phased rollout rationale
nodes.rationale: Model first (no risk until migration runs), backends in parallel (no immediate switching), views one type at a time, mask/asset support on top (disableable), comprehensive tests before prod.

nodes.label: CI backend job (standalone test modules + schema validate)
nodes.rationale: Python 3.12; installs gcc/python3-dev because psutil builds from source on some runners; auto-discovers services/tests/test_*.py; DEBUG=1 so the secret-key fail-fast doesn't trip.
nodes.norm_label: ci backend job (standalone test modules + schema validate)

nodes.label: CI installs a mediapipe-free requirements subset
nodes.rationale: mediapipe is only imported inside services/orientation.py at call time; no test or boot path touches it, so excluding the ~200 MB dependency keeps the job fast.
nodes.norm_label: ci installs a mediapipe-free requirements subset

nodes.label: CI validates OpenAPI schema with --fail-on-warn
nodes.rationale: Schema is generated from @extend_schema so a defect never fails a test — it quietly ships a wrong document. A warning means a view was dropped or an operationId collided, which makes the reference wrong not untidy.

nodes.label: CI frontend job (pnpm typecheck / lint / jest --ci)
nodes.rationale: pnpm 9.15.9 set up before setup-node so caching finds it; matches the frontend Dockerfile corepack version; Node 20.
nodes.norm_label: ci frontend job (pnpm typecheck / lint / jest --ci)

nodes.label: CI concurrency: newer push cancels in-flight run per ref
nodes.norm_label: ci concurrency: newer push cancels in-flight run per ref

nodes.label: x-default-logging anchor (json-file 50m × 3)
nodes.rationale: Without it Docker's json-file driver writes unbounded and a noisy week can fill the disk. Every service inherits it.

nodes.label: proxy service (nginx:1.27-alpine)
nodes.rationale: TLS terminates here with a Cloudflare Origin Certificate; nginx.conf is a single-file bind mount (inode trap); depends on backend healthy; /nginx-health probe.

nodes.label: redis service (durable broker)
nodes.rationale: noeviction + appendonly everysec, 512 MB cap, redis_data volume; hostname kept as `redis` so REDIS_URL and stale prod .env keep working.

nodes.label: redis-cache service (disposable Django cache)
nodes.rationale: allkeys-lru, 256 MB cap, no volume — cache is rebuildable and can never touch the broker.

nodes.label: db service (postgres:16-alpine, tuned)
nodes.rationale: shared_buffers 128MB, work_mem 8MB (default 4 MB too small for any real JOIN/sort), effective_cache_size 384MB, log_min_duration_statement 1000 for free slow-query observability. Loopback-only port.

nodes.label: backend service (Django + gunicorn)
nodes.rationale: Loopback-only :8000 — all traffic via nginx; 2 GB limit so one leaking worker can't OOM the container; healthcheck hits /api/health; ./storage bind-mounted.

nodes.label: frontend service (Next.js standalone)
nodes.rationale: AUTH_SECRET uses ${VAR:?} so a missing secret aborts the deploy loudly instead of shipping a forgeable session key; healthcheck uses 127.0.0.1 because alpine wget resolves localhost to ::1 while Next binds IPv4 only.

nodes.label: celery-worker-standard service
nodes.rationale: The only worker; CELERY_QUEUE=priority,standard; CELERY_CONCURRENCY deliberately unset (auto-detect from CPU); 2 GB limit; healthcheck pings the worker through the broker so it also fails when the broker connection is wedged — visibility only, compose does not auto-heal.

nodes.label: Loopback-only host port publishing (Phase 4)
nodes.rationale: Docker port publishing bypasses host firewalls, so 0.0.0.0 would expose Postgres/Django/Next directly to the internet on prod. Host tooling connects via localhost.

nodes.label: Design: three structural changes
nodes.rationale: LayoutCatalogue replaces storage/layouts/*.json; S3Storage replaces the commented-out stub (list_layouts queries Postgres not S3); asset_store.py provides typed calendar asset reads via StorageBackend.read_calendar_asset. LocalStorage stays default for dev.

nodes.label: Design: pre-migration current state
nodes.rationale: Views called storage.layouts_dir()/masks_dir() then raw open(), bypassing StorageBackend; STORAGE_BACKEND=s3 raised NotImplementedError; latest migration 0015; cache prefix pe:.

nodes.label: Design: LayoutCatalogue field table
nodes.rationale: name CharField(255) unique case-sensitive overrides definition['name']; product_type inferred from definition.productType default single_canvas; version bumped per write; imported_at/imported_by co-validated in clean(). Composite indexes (product_type,is_deprecated) and (is_deprecated,is_public).

nodes.label: Design: S3Storage backend
nodes.rationale: Layouts from Postgres, masks/uploads/exports/ops-config in S3; __init__ raises ImproperlyConfigured naming missing env vars; boto3 client.

nodes.label: Design: services/asset_store.py read_asset
nodes.rationale: _VALID_ASSET_TYPES frozenset; ValueError on unknown type; delegates to get_storage().read_calendar_asset; callers CalendarStylesView, HolidaysView, _read_fonts.

nodes.label: Design: error handling table
nodes.rationale: 404 on DoesNotExist; 500 without internal detail; cache failures log and never fail the request; path guard 400 before DB/S3; S3 mask errors 502; calendar asset S3 miss falls back to local; missing prod_layouts.json → warn and succeed with zero rows.

nodes.label: Property 1: cache invalidation completeness
nodes.rationale: Invalidation always attempted after a write even if the write raised; list caches deleted even when the detail pattern delete fails. Validates Req 7.1, 7.5, 7.6.

nodes.label: Property 2: rename atomicity
nodes.rationale: select_for_update on the old row inside transaction.atomic so no request observes old and new both non-deprecated. Validates Req 6.7, 6.8.

nodes.label: Property 3: migration idempotency
nodes.rationale: update_or_create(name=...) so applying 0016 twice leaves the same row set. Validates Req 2.2, 11.1.

nodes.label: Property 4: STORAGE_BACKEND=local full bypass
nodes.rationale: Claims that with STORAGE_BACKEND=local no LayoutCatalogue query is issued and reads fall through to the filesystem. CLAUDE.md ('Views query LayoutCatalogue first; no fallback to disk') and the runbook ('fallback to filesystem not implemented') contradict this — the property was designed but not shipped.

nodes.label: Property 5: mask copy-before-delete
nodes.rationale: Never delete a mask key before a successful copy; copy failure → 500 with original untouched; delete failure after copy → orphan logged, 200.

nodes.label: Property 6: JSON round-trip fidelity
nodes.rationale: JSONField preserves Unicode, nesting and floats; definition_in == definition_out.

nodes.label: Design: cache key reference (unchanged)
nodes.rationale: layouts_list_all (ListLayoutsView), ops_layouts_list_all (LayoutManagementView.get), layout_detail:{name}:{surfaces} (GetLayoutView, EditorInitView); all 120 s; all invalidated by invalidate_layout_caches.

nodes.label: Design: testing strategy
nodes.rationale: Unit tests with moto for S3; integration roundtrip POST ops/layouts → GET layouts; cache warming via editor/init; data-migration test against a staging dump; smoke tests.

nodes.label: Design Phase 6: .gitignore storage dirs
nodes.rationale: Ignore storage/layouts, masks, calendar_styles, calendar_palettes, holidays to break the git-conflict cycle; prod_layouts.json IS committed as the data handoff artifact.

nodes.label: Design: layout read/write and mask serve flows
nodes.rationale: Read: guard → cache → LayoutCatalogue.get → surfaces filter → cache.set. Write: guard → json.loads → validate → update_or_create → mask upload → invalidate caches. Mask: guard → file_exists → presigned URL (302).
nodes.norm_label: design: layout read/write and mask serve flows

nodes.label: Requirements: why migrate layouts off git-tracked files
nodes.rationale: Git-tracked layout JSON rewritten by the ops UI at runtime causes perpetual merge conflicts and broken deployments; moving to Postgres + S3 with a StorageBackend switch breaks the cycle while preserving API contracts so no frontend change is needed.
nodes.norm_label: requirements: why migrate layouts off git-tracked files

nodes.label: Req 1: LayoutCatalogue data model
nodes.rationale: Fields, case-sensitive byte-for-byte unique name, indexes, auto timestamps, imported_at/imported_by co-validation.

nodes.label: Req 2: Migration 0016 schema + idempotent import
nodes.rationale: update_or_create per entry; malformed entries logged and skipped; NOP reverse; missing prod_layouts.json → warn and succeed; non-array root → error and skip.

nodes.label: Req 3: S3Storage backend
nodes.rationale: Fail-fast ImproperlyConfigured on missing AWS vars; implements every StorageBackend method; list_layouts never LISTs S3; multipart assemble with abort on failure.

nodes.label: Req 4: ListLayoutsView serves from DB
nodes.rationale: Merge definition + name + hasCalendar; layouts_list_all cached 120 s; ?fields=summary; always {layouts: [...]}; DB error → 500 with detail.

nodes.label: Req 5: GetLayoutView serves from DB
nodes.rationale: Path guard first (400 before any query); 404 on miss; layout_detail:{name}:{surfaces} cached 120 s; surfaces filter case-insensitive, empty array not 404.

nodes.label: Req 6: LayoutManagementView writes to DB
nodes.rationale: update_or_create returns 200/201; soft-delete sets is_deprecated; rename atomic in one transaction with 409 on conflict; invalidate caches after every write.

nodes.label: Req 7: atomic cache invalidation
nodes.rationale: Bulk-delete both list keys together; delete layout_detail:{name}:* pattern; AttributeError → fallback to unparameterised key; other exceptions logged, never propagated.

nodes.label: Req 8: mask serving via presigned URLs
nodes.rationale: S3: 301 to presigned URL with 300–3600 s expiry; local: 200 with file; guard first; 404 on missing; 502 on other S3 errors without detail.
nodes.norm_label: req 8: mask serving via presigned urls

nodes.label: Req 9: mask upload to S3 and rename copy-before-delete
nodes.norm_label: req 9: mask upload to s3 and rename copy-before-delete

nodes.label: Req 10: calendar assets under ops-config/ with local fallback
nodes.norm_label: req 10: calendar assets under ops-config/ with local fallback

nodes.label: Req 11: deployment and rollback
nodes.rationale: Migration applies automatically on container start; STORAGE_BACKEND=local claimed to restore filesystem behaviour without DB rollback (not implemented per runbook); reverse is NOP.

nodes.label: Req 12: API contract preservation
nodes.rationale: Identical response shapes and status codes; masks endpoint stays on the embed allowlist without a privilege gate.

nodes.label: Path_Traversal_Guard (_is_safe_layout_name)
nodes.rationale: Rejects names containing /, \, .., or a leading .; always the first validation step before any DB or S3 call.

nodes.label: Soft_Delete via is_deprecated
nodes.rationale: Preserves audit trail while hiding from public reads.

nodes.label: Storage migration deployment runbook
nodes.rationale: Pre-deploy export on prod, commit dump, optional S3 creds (keep STORAGE_BACKEND=local), ./deploy.sh both, verify 0016, post-deploy checks, ~1 h total during low traffic.

nodes.label: Runbook: export prod layout catalogue before 0016
nodes.rationale: Run export_layout_catalogue.py against storage/layouts on prod, verify count matches filesystem, scp and commit backend/migrations/prod_layouts.json.
nodes.norm_label: runbook: export prod layout catalogue before 0016

nodes.label: Runbook: post-deployment verification
nodes.rationale: LayoutCatalogue count, sample layout lookup, /api/layouts and /api/ops/layouts curls, embed session creation, both smoke tests.

nodes.label: Runbook: rollback plan
nodes.rationale: Option 1 (STORAGE_BACKEND=local) is only partial — views still query LayoutCatalogue and a filesystem fallback is not implemented; full rollback needs git revert + backup restore.

nodes.label: Pillow==10.3.0
nodes.rationale: pillow-heif is pinned to the release that resolves against Pillow 10.3.0 — do NOT bump Pillow to chase a newer pillow-heif without re-testing the render pipeline.

nodes.label: pillow-heif==0.22.0
nodes.rationale: Bundles libheif 1.19 as a manylinux wheel. Exists because browser-side heic2any (2021 libheif) cannot read iOS 18 tmap gain-map HEIC and Chrome/Firefox have no HEIC codec; used by services/heic.py behind POST /api/heic/convert.

nodes.label: mediapipe==0.10.18
nodes.rationale: Loaded lazily by services/orientation.py for POST /api/orientation/detect; ~200 MB docker layer (tflite-runtime, opencv-headless, numpy, protobuf); workers install it but never import it.

nodes.label: Doc status taxonomy (current / shipped / not started / removed)
nodes.rationale: Most of docs/ is not current-state reference; reading a shipped PRD as documentation is the main way to get a wrong answer. Each doc gets a status so a PRD with no status is not read as a description of the present.
nodes.norm_label: doc status taxonomy (current / shipped / not started / removed)

nodes.label: Where a doc and the code disagree, the code wins
nodes.rationale: Docs are not in CI; nothing checks their claims. CLAUDE.md is the maintained architectural reference and wins over the docs folder on any disagreement.
nodes.norm_label: where a doc and the code disagree, the code wins

nodes.label: Every doc gets a status line
nodes.rationale: CALENDAR_FEATURE_PRD.md spent a month claiming 'Proposal' for a shipped feature because it had no status line.
nodes.norm_label: every doc gets a status line

nodes.label: Don't rewrite history to match the present
nodes.rationale: Version-history tables and completed action items are an audit trail; corrections go in a new row and superseded docs are marked, not edited.
nodes.norm_label: don't rewrite history to match the present

nodes.label: printo-architecture-audit/ removed 2026-09-07
nodes.rationale: The 12-part audit covered the wider Printo estate, not this codebase, could not be verified from this checkout, and would only drift from the server lead's copy. Recoverable at git show 13430c7.

nodes.label: Four markdown files deliberately outside docs/
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and README.md must sit at the repo root for tooling/GitHub; scalar/README.md is provenance for a vendored bundle and belongs beside it.
nodes.norm_label: four markdown files deliberately outside docs/

nodes.label: Inter-Variable.ttf
nodes.rationale: One well-engineered variable font (weights 100-900 in a single 859 KB file, Apache 2.0 / SIL OFL) serves every weight; bundled in the Docker image under services/fonts_assets/.

nodes.label: Single bundled font, no font picker (PRD §11.7)
nodes.rationale: Hardcoding one font eliminates a class of production failure modes (font missing, preview/print drift) and removes the need for a picker for ops or customers.
nodes.norm_label: single bundled font, no font picker (prd §11.7)

nodes.label: Fallback to PIL default bitmap font
nodes.rationale: If the .ttf is absent the renderer still ships output, just with ugly text, and logs a warning — degrade rather than fail the render.
nodes.norm_label: fallback to pil default bitmap font

nodes.label: Boot-time startup_check() for missing font
nodes.rationale: Flags a missing font in the Django log at boot so deploys never silently degrade.

nodes.label: SIL Open Font License 1.1
nodes.rationale: OFL §1-3 explicitly permit bundling the .ttf in the Docker image and shipping it inside rendered PNGs.

nodes.label: Contract if a font picker is ever added
nodes.rationale: Would reverse §11.7: read names from storage/fonts.json, resolve each to <FamilyName>.ttf in fonts_assets/, and add a startup check that every JSON entry has a matching .ttf. Until then any extra .ttf is dead weight.
nodes.norm_label: contract if a font picker is ever added

nodes.label: Calendar feature — S3-readiness audit
nodes.rationale: Conclusion: READY — no hardcoded local paths outside settings.STORAGE_ROOT, so no code changes are needed to make the calendar feature S3-ready; migration is gated only on a blob-store shim covering atomic writes.

nodes.label: STORAGE_ROOT env var
nodes.rationale: Single env-driven root (default ./storage) from which LAYOUTS_DIR, EXPORTS_DIR and UPLOADS_DIR derive, so redirecting one variable redirects every path.

nodes.label: storage/fonts.json (FONTS_JSON_PATH)
nodes.rationale: Font .ttf files ship with the image under services/fonts_assets/, not under STORAGE_ROOT — correct because fonts are immutable assets.

nodes.label: Local-filesystem atomic writes — the single S3 blocker
nodes.rationale: Three callers do tempfile + os.replace atomic writes. S3 PutObject is already atomic per object, so each becomes write-temp → upload → delete, or boto3.upload_fileobj.
nodes.norm_label: local-filesystem atomic writes — the single s3 blocker

nodes.label: LayoutEngine._write_output_atomic
nodes.rationale: Stages the temp file in the same directory as the final output so it stays within STORAGE_ROOT.

nodes.label: RenderJobDownloadView ZIP built under EXPORTS_DIR
nodes.rationale: The temp ZIP lives under EXPORTS_DIR so it inherits whatever backing store STORAGE_ROOT points at.

nodes.label: services/blob_store.py shim (proposed)
nodes.rationale: Wrap reads (open → boto3.get_object) and writes behind one shim so the three callers stay unchanged during the S3 move.

nodes.label: No hardcoded paths outside STORAGE_ROOT
nodes.rationale: Repo-wide grep for /app/storage/, /tmp/storage/, /var/... returns zero hits in source; only test scripts and tempfile defaults use /tmp, which is S3-compatible.

nodes.label: printo.in storefront — pe-callback integration guide
nodes.rationale: The only doc with an external audience (printo.in's storefront team). Source of truth is notify_caller_webhook_task; if the doc disagrees, the task wins.

nodes.label: Product Editor is a standalone print-file generator
nodes.rationale: It does not push files into Printo's OMS or any other backend; the storefront's webhook handler is what completes delivery.
nodes.norm_label: product editor is a standalone print-file generator

nodes.label: POST <callback_url> webhook (pe-callback)
nodes.rationale: Fired when a render completes; the storefront verifies the signature, fetches the ZIP and attaches it to the order.

nodes.label: X-Signature: sha256=<hex> (HMAC-SHA256 of raw body, api_key as secret)
nodes.rationale: No domain allowlist on callback_url — auth is enforced by the api_key the caller already holds, and the HMAC lets the caller verify the request really came from Product Editor.
nodes.norm_label: x-signature: sha256=<hex> (hmac-sha256 of raw body, api_key as secret)

nodes.label: Webhook success payload
nodes.rationale: order_id, job_id, status, download_url, print_download_url, mock_download_url, uploads_download_url, expires_at, file_count, layout_name, export_format.

nodes.label: Webhook failure payload
nodes.rationale: Sent best-effort after retries are exhausted: order_id, job_id, status=failed, error, layout_name.

nodes.label: download_url — combined archive
nodes.rationale: 1_customer_uploads/ + 2_mock/ + 3_print/ in folders; unchanged from v1.8 and not deprecated so existing callers need no migration.

nodes.label: print_download_url (?content=print)
nodes.rationale: 300 DPI print files flat at the archive root.

nodes.label: mock_download_url (?content=mock)
nodes.rationale: Small web preview JPEGs, flat — the small, fast archive.

nodes.label: uploads_download_url (?content=uploads)
nodes.rationale: null when the session was created with include_uploads=false — nothing is behind it, so it is not advertised; callers must guard for null.

nodes.label: ?content= filter on one download endpoint
nodes.rationale: The split archives are served by filtering the same rendered files; nothing is duplicated on disk. Added Aug 2026 for storefronts that keep mock and print in separate fields.

nodes.label: Single-part archives are flat at the root
nodes.rationale: A folder containing only one kind of file is just an extra level to walk; the combined archive keeps its three numbered folders exactly as before.
nodes.norm_label: single-part archives are flat at the root

nodes.label: 404 on mock_download_url instead of an empty ZIP
nodes.rationale: Returned deliberately when no previews could be generated so the storefront never stores a 22-byte archive against an order.
nodes.norm_label: 404 on mock_download_url instead of an empty zip

nodes.label: Webhook retry: 6 attempts, 2^n backoff
nodes.rationale: Any non-2xx response is a delivery failure; 1 initial + 5 retries at 1,2,4,8,16 s (max_retries=5 on notify_caller_webhook_task).

nodes.label: GET *_download_url with Authorization: Bearer <api_key>
nodes.rationale: Same key the storefront uses to create embed sessions — no new credential needed.

nodes.label: Verify HMAC against the RAW body
nodes.rationale: express.json() / request.data re-serialise the body so the HMAC never matches; mount express.raw() first and verify against the Buffer / request.body.
nodes.norm_label: verify hmac against the raw body

nodes.label: Constant-time signature comparison
nodes.rationale: crypto.timingSafeEqual / hmac.compare_digest instead of === to avoid timing attacks.

nodes.label: Fetch the ZIP out-of-band, return 200 fast
nodes.rationale: Product Editor has a 10 s webhook timeout and retries up to 6 attempts; a synchronous download in the handler causes timeouts and duplicate downstream work.
nodes.norm_label: fetch the zip out-of-band, return 200 fast

nodes.label: Stream the ZIP to disk/S3, never buffer
nodes.rationale: Combined archives run 30-500 MB; buffering in memory OOMs the handler.
nodes.norm_label: stream the zip to disk/s3, never buffer

nodes.label: PRODUCT_EDITOR_API_KEY env var
nodes.rationale: Shared secret for HMAC verification and Bearer for the ZIP fetch; read from env so rotation does not silently break the integration.

nodes.label: callback_url on POST /api/embed/session
nodes.rationale: Must be https:// and <= 2000 chars; flows through the embed proxy, is stamped onto CanvasData, and is the exact URL the webhook task POSTs to.

nodes.label: qty on POST /api/embed/session
nodes.rationale: Whole number 1..10000; omitted means nothing is enforced. Stored on the session and injected as a header the browser never sees, so the customer cannot raise it by editing the URL.

nodes.label: qty validation rules (400 at session creation)
nodes.rationale: Numeric strings and integral floats are accepted because JSON has no int/float distinction and form values arrive as strings; 0 is an error, not 'unlimited', because it would cap every order at nothing; true is rejected as a caller bug.
nodes.norm_label: qty validation rules (400 at session creation)

nodes.label: Over-qty blocked twice, under-qty allowed with warnings
nodes.rationale: qty comes from the caller; a hard gate in both directions would let one wrong value strand a real order at checkout. Over-count is rejected by the editor modal AND by POST /api/editor/render with 400.
nodes.norm_label: over-qty blocked twice, under-qty allowed with warnings

nodes.label: Legacy ?qty=N URL param still read, never enforced
nodes.rationale: Rollout fallback: the editor uses the session value when present and the URL value otherwise; nothing server-side honours the URL param because it is browser-editable.
nodes.norm_label: legacy ?qty=n url param still read, never enforced

nodes.label: qty applies to single-surface products only
nodes.rationale: Two-sided products, calendars and books have a surface count fixed by the layout, which qty does not describe.
nodes.norm_label: qty applies to single-surface products only

nodes.label: Re-check file_count on the completion webhook
nodes.rationale: The only guarantee of a delivered count, since under-upload is deliberately not blocked.
nodes.norm_label: re-check file_count on the completion webhook

nodes.label: Allow inbound HTTPS from Product Editor egress to pe-callback
nodes.norm_label: allow inbound https from product editor egress to pe-callback

nodes.label: Local testing via ngrok tunnel + signed test payload
nodes.norm_label: local testing via ngrok tunnel + signed test payload

nodes.label: pe:render_job postMessage to parent
nodes.rationale: UX-only ('your design is being prepared'); file delivery happens via the webhook. targetOrigin is strictly locked, never '*'.

nodes.label: AI Guardrails — Product Editor
nodes.rationale: Short list of rules that exist because breaking them has already cost something; companion to CLAUDE.md, which wins on any disagreement.

nodes.label: No AI image manipulation
nodes.rationale: Background removal, product detection and generative editing stay out of scope; the one sanctioned ML feature is auto-orientation, which only reads a photo and persists nothing.

nodes.label: Auto-orientation via MediaPipe Pose (POST /api/orientation/detect)
nodes.rationale: Runs inline in a Gunicorn thread (~30-150 ms) — the one deliberate exception to 'large image work goes to Celery' because generateCanvases needs the rotation before drawing the preview.

nodes.label: Materialized surfaces (calendar template → 12 month-surfaces)
nodes.rationale: A change to surface handling must be checked against the materialize path as well as plain front/back layouts.

nodes.label: TypeScript full strict mode
nodes.rationale: Unclosed template literals in JSX className cause ~17 cascade errors; run pnpm typecheck before pushing.

nodes.label: No direct DOM manipulation
nodes.rationale: React owns the DOM; mutating nodes underneath it desyncs the virtual DOM and innerHTML is an XSS sink. Exempt: off-screen canvases, Fabric roots via useRef, transient <a> downloads, window/document listeners with cleanup.

nodes.label: Path safety (_is_path_safe)
nodes.rationale: Every request-derived file path must be validated to prevent traversal.

nodes.label: LayoutEngine must receive layout_definition from LayoutCatalogue
nodes.rationale: Missing layout_definition causes [Errno 2] No such file or directory on render; LayoutEngine must never load layouts from disk itself. Four call sites were wrong on 2026-09-04.
nodes.norm_label: layoutengine must receive layout_definition from layoutcatalogue

nodes.label: Ops asset writes go through storage.write_calendar_asset()
nodes.rationale: Direct open()/os.remove() writes are invisible to S3-backed deployments and lost on container restart; _write_fonts/_write_calendar_style/_write_holidays all route through the abstraction since 2026-09-04.
nodes.norm_label: ops asset writes go through storage.write_calendar_asset()

nodes.label: Large image work runs in Celery workers, not Gunicorn
nodes.rationale: Workers are capped at 2 GB per replica with concurrency auto-detected from CPU count; scale out with --scale rather than raising per-replica concurrency because Pillow compositing is the memory consumer.
nodes.norm_label: large image work runs in celery workers, not gunicorn

nodes.label: Never mix autoretry_for and self.retry()
nodes.rationale: The codebase uses self.retry(exc, countdown) exclusively so the DB retry_count and Celery's internal counter stay in sync.

nodes.label: MemoryError and SoftTimeLimitExceeded skip retries
nodes.rationale: The worker is out of memory or time; retrying would immediately fail again, so the job is marked failed at once.

nodes.label: Caller webhook is a separate Celery task
nodes.rationale: Never call callback_url inside render_canvas_task: it must not block the render slot and must retry independently (up to 5x). Only dispatched when canvas.callback_url is set.
nodes.norm_label: caller webhook is a separate celery task

nodes.label: callback_url stored on CanvasData at submission
nodes.rationale: Propagated from EmbedSession via the X-Callback-URL header, not passed through the task chain; the webhook task reads it from the DB.
nodes.norm_label: callback_url stored on canvasdata at submission

nodes.label: Task dispatch inside transaction.on_commit()
nodes.rationale: Dispatching inside an open DB transaction lets the worker start before the row is committed.

nodes.label: Redis failure on dispatch must fail the job immediately
nodes.rationale: The on_commit handler catches the dispatch exception and sets RenderJob.status='failed'; a job must never sit silently in 'queued'.
nodes.norm_label: redis failure on dispatch must fail the job immediately

nodes.label: celery-beat must not run DB migrations
nodes.rationale: Only the Gunicorn/backend container runs migrate --noinput, eliminating concurrent-migration races.
nodes.norm_label: celery-beat must not run db migrations

nodes.label: All three tasks route to the standard queue
nodes.norm_label: all three tasks route to the standard queue

nodes.label: priority queue has no producer; the one worker drains it anyway
nodes.rationale: The second worker for the CMYK express path was removed Aug 2026 having never executed a task. Listening to both queues closes the trap where apply_async(queue='priority') would sit in Redis forever. It is NOT a QoS tier — Celery round-robins across -Q queues.
nodes.norm_label: priority queue has no producer; the one worker drains it anyway

nodes.label: GC skips requires_manual_review orders
nodes.rationale: garbage_collector_task must call _is_manual_review_path before deleting any file.

nodes.label: GC soft_time_limit=3300 / time_limit=3600
nodes.rationale: A hung sweep can never permanently occupy a worker slot.

nodes.label: Poison-pill guard counts only broker redeliveries
nodes.rationale: A worker crash under acks_late redelivers the SAME message (redelivered=True, retries frozen) whereas self.retry() publishes a NEW one; conflating them would abort healthy jobs after normal retries.
nodes.norm_label: poison-pill guard counts only broker redeliveries

nodes.label: Never requests.post a customer callback_url directly
nodes.rationale: post_webhook_safely pins the socket to the pre-validated IP so DNS cannot rebind between validation and send, and sets allow_redirects=False.
nodes.norm_label: never requests.post a customer callback_url directly

nodes.label: LayoutManagementView rename = soft-delete then create
nodes.rationale: Preserves the audit trail and avoids race conditions versus in-place mutation; masks migrate atomically in the same transaction.

nodes.label: Mask uploads go to masks/{filename}, not save_upload()
nodes.rationale: save_upload() routes to uploads/_no_order/; masks use a direct S3 put or LocalStorage.masks_dir().
nodes.norm_label: mask uploads go to masks/{filename}, not save_upload()

nodes.label: Re-creating a deprecated layout un-deprecates it
nodes.rationale: update_or_create passes is_deprecated=False in defaults so 'create a deleted layout again' makes it public.
nodes.norm_label: re-creating a deprecated layout un-deprecates it

nodes.label: CanvasData written via update_or_create(order_id=...)
nodes.rationale: Operator retries and customer resubmissions must not crash with a unique-constraint error.

nodes.label: celery_task_id is nullable, never ''
nodes.rationale: Set to None at creation and populated after enqueue.

nodes.label: Embed proxy allowlist is path AND method
nodes.rationale: Prefix-only until 2026-09-03: fonts/holidays/calendar-styles accept ops writes upstream and the proxy injects the session's real (ops-flagged DIRECT) api_key, so an embed token could PUT holiday data. Never add a prefix without naming its methods.
nodes.norm_label: embed proxy allowlist is path and method

nodes.label: Never git reset --hard or checkout -- storage/ on prod
nodes.rationale: storage/ layouts, masks and fonts.json are git-tracked AND rewritten by the ops UI; prod has diverged (20 deleted, 11 renamed). Either command resurrects the obsolete catalogue beside the live one.
nodes.norm_label: never git reset --hard or checkout -- storage/ on prod

nodes.label: Don't raise DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE to fix autosave 400s
nodes.rationale: 37% of autosaves 400 because editor_state embeds base64 previews averaging 16 MB; raising the limit makes gunicorn buffer those per request on a 2-core, 2 GB-capped box — silent save failures become OOM. Shrink the payload instead.
nodes.norm_label: don't raise data_upload_max_memory_size to fix autosave 400s

nodes.label: A handler without @extend_schema is dropped from the API reference
nodes.rationale: drf-spectacular logs 'unable to guess serializer' and renders the operation with no body; request= and responses= must be explicit.
nodes.norm_label: a handler without @extend_schema is dropped from the api reference

nodes.label: Auth schemes live in api/schema.py, not SPECTACULAR_SETTINGS
nodes.rationale: SECURITY_DEFINITIONS is a drf-yasg key silently ignored by drf-spectacular, leaving BearerAuth undefined and the Authorize dropdown empty.
nodes.norm_label: auth schemes live in api/schema.py, not spectacular_settings

nodes.label: FontsView/CalendarStylesView/HolidaysView must set auth= per operation
nodes.rationale: They are AllowAny with the ops check inside the handler, so the generator would advertise destructive methods as needing no credentials.
nodes.norm_label: fontsview/calendarstylesview/holidaysview must set auth= per operation

nodes.label: Validate the schema with manage.py spectacular --validate --fail-on-warn
nodes.rationale: Not covered by CI and the image bakes source via COPY, so build first.
nodes.norm_label: validate the schema with manage.py spectacular --validate --fail-on-warn

nodes.label: Dispose Fabric canvases and revoke Object URLs
nodes.norm_label: dispose fabric canvases and revoke object urls

nodes.label: isExport flag gates frame outlines and preview overlays
nodes.rationale: Both FabricEditor.tsx and fabric-renderer.ts must respect it or outlines appear in downloads.
nodes.norm_label: isexport flag gates frame outlines and preview overlays

nodes.label: Qty: hard cap going over, warn-and-proceed going under
nodes.rationale: qty is supplied by the caller; a wrong value must not strand a real order. qty_violation has one '>' and no lower bound. Two mirrored homes: checkOrderQty (TS) and services/order_qty.py. The server half is narrower (exempts calendars/books) and fails open.
nodes.norm_label: qty: hard cap going over, warn-and-proceed going under

nodes.label: qty lives on EmbedSession, not the iframe URL
nodes.rationale: Flows caller → session row → embed-proxy cache → X-Order-Qty → Django; a header the proxy injects must also be in its cached tuple or it vanishes for 110 minutes.
nodes.norm_label: qty lives on embedsession, not the iframe url

nodes.label: 'Add Files' appends, never replaces
nodes.rationale: A native <input type=file> pick is not cumulative; feeding the raw pick into setFiles() wiped every earlier canvas (live bug until PR #24). Multi-surface layouts are excluded from the merge.

nodes.label: Low-res DPI warning stays non-blocking
nodes.rationale: dpi-utils.ts mirrors the placement maths of both renderers; change either and the warning lies. DPI_WARN=150 / DPI_CRITICAL=100, strict <.

nodes.label: No CMYK / ICC soft-proof warnings
nodes.rationale: The RGB→CMYK→RGB pipeline was removed in v1.8; colour is handled invisibly by services/image_loader.py (ICC→sRGB at load, sRGB-tagged output). Never Image.open().convert('RGBA') a customer photo directly — it discards the profile.

nodes.label: A layout's identifier is its filename stem
nodes.rationale: When name field and filename diverged in case (classic_A4.json / 'classic_a4') the layout became unopenable on production Linux only — the dev Mac is case-insensitive. (Superseded by LayoutCatalogue.name as of PR #111; the case-sensitivity lesson stands.)
nodes.norm_label: a layout's identifier is its filename stem

nodes.label: Don't cross the editor_state / render_state streams
nodes.rationale: editor_state is frontend-owned (CanvasStateView autosave); render_state is pipeline-owned (EditorRenderView at submit). As one field the two writers clobbered each other: submit wiped autosaves and a post-submit autosave could strip a queued job's payload.
nodes.norm_label: don't cross the editor_state / render_state streams

nodes.label: CanvasStateView.put keeps image_paths out of update_or_create defaults
nodes.rationale: Writing image_paths or [] there blanked recorded paths every 2 s, making DPDP erasure report files_deleted: 0 while photos stayed on disk (0011). Model default=list (0013) keeps INSERT working since a model default applies on INSERT only.
nodes.norm_label: canvasstateview.put keeps image_paths out of update_or_create defaults

nodes.label: Run migrations only from the backend (Gunicorn) container
nodes.rationale: Every CanvasData field change needs a migration; never migrate from a worker or beat container.
nodes.norm_label: run migrations only from the backend (gunicorn) container

nodes.label: PRD: Product Editor — End-to-End Production Automation (v1.13)
nodes.rationale: Business/product PRD: problem statement, TAT targets, success metrics, rollout decision framework. §8.0 is the live open-items list; §8.1/§8.2 are history.
nodes.norm_label: prd: product editor — end-to-end production automation (v1.13)

nodes.label: Manual design-preflight checkpoint is the bottleneck
nodes.rationale: Not image generation or print execution: every order passes a manual review of file quality and count versus ordered quantity, and stalls when the customer is slow to respond. Exists because the legacy system had no customer preview or automatic validation.
nodes.norm_label: manual design-preflight checkpoint is the bottleneck

nodes.label: Target TAT: < 5 min upload → production-ready
nodes.rationale: Down from ~1 h (store pickup / express) and 2-3 h (standard delivery).

nodes.label: Store pickup & express: same-day / 4-6 h SLA
nodes.norm_label: store pickup & express: same-day / 4-6 h sla

nodes.label: Standard delivery: 3 PM daily courier cutoff
nodes.rationale: Late-cleared orders miss dispatch and slip a full day.
nodes.norm_label: standard delivery: 3 pm daily courier cutoff

nodes.label: Preflight team is a fixed-capacity single point of failure
