nodes.rationale: Cannot scale linearly with volume; inconsistent judgement between operators; understaffing stalls the whole pipeline.
nodes.norm_label: preflight team is a fixed-capacity single point of failure

nodes.label: A1 — Customer-facing preview before checkout
nodes.rationale: Customer self-validates by approving the visual preview; empty frames plus auto-fill / pick-to-fill replace the manual count check.

nodes.label: Low-resolution detection (~150 effective DPI)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately non-blocking — informs, never refuses the order. Replaced preflight's 'is this file good enough?' judgement; mirrors placement maths in both renderers (dpi-utils.ts).

nodes.label: Empty-surface and duplicate-fill warnings (submit-guards.ts)
nodes.rationale: Catch a blank side on a two-sided product and unintended repeats; qty auto-fill is exempt because repetition there is intentional. Warn-and-proceed.

nodes.label: Colour handled invisibly instead of a CMYK warning
nodes.rationale: The ICC-calibrated CMYK soft-proof pipeline was removed in v1.8; image_loader.py colour-manages ICC→sRGB on load so Display-P3 / AdobeRGB / CMYK-tagged photos stop shifting without the customer knowing what a profile is.
nodes.norm_label: colour handled invisibly instead of a cmyk warning

nodes.label: A2 — Direct-to-production file delivery (post-checkout)
nodes.rationale: 300 DPI server render delivered via the embed webhook (primary) or direct download (fallback); no manual handoff.

nodes.label: Direct download fallback (poll render-status, fetch ZIP)
nodes.norm_label: direct download fallback (poll render-status, fetch zip)

nodes.label: No internal OMS push (standalone generator)
nodes.rationale: push_to_production_estimator_task and OMS_PRODUCTION_ESTIMATOR_URL were retired in v1.9: the webhook gives the storefront everything it needs and it talks to OMS through its own integration.

nodes.label: A2.1 — Embed integration sequence (session → iframe → render → webhook → ZIP)
nodes.norm_label: a2.1 — embed integration sequence (session → iframe → render → webhook → zip)

nodes.label: B1 — Canvas state persistence (done Apr 27, 2026)
nodes.rationale: Two layers: server editor_state JSON (autosave 2 s) plus IndexedDB blobs keyed (orderId, fileId) because Files do not serialise. Quota: ~1 GB free space for 200 photos; very large jobs best submitted in one session.

nodes.label: B2 — Async image generation queue (done Apr 5, 2026)
nodes.rationale: Synchronous rendering held a Gunicorn thread for the whole render, causing timeouts under festival peaks; Celery + Redis returns a job id immediately.
nodes.norm_label: b2 — async image generation queue (done apr 5, 2026)

nodes.label: Dedicated priority worker (PRD-era description)
nodes.rationale: The PRD table describes a dormant dedicated priority worker; AI_GUARDRAILS records it was removed Aug 2026 and the single worker drains both queues — the PRD row is stale.

nodes.label: Render retry: 3 retries, 2/4/8 s; MemoryError & soft limit skip
nodes.norm_label: render retry: 3 retries, 2/4/8 s; memoryerror & soft limit skip

nodes.label: Render-status polling with Redis cache (3 s queued / 300 s terminal)
nodes.norm_label: render-status polling with redis cache (3 s queued / 300 s terminal)

nodes.label: Per-job UUID subdirectories under EXPORTS_DIR
nodes.rationale: Prevents simultaneous renders of the same layout overwriting each other's outputs; GC removes empty dirs afterwards.

nodes.label: API key baked into the client bundle (NEXT_PUBLIC_DIRECT_API_KEY)
nodes.rationale: Extractable from DevTools; fixed by routing all dashboard/editor calls through the server-side /api/internal/proxy with a server-only INTERNAL_API_KEY.
nodes.norm_label: api key baked into the client bundle (next_public_direct_api_key)

nodes.label: PIA token refresh (RefreshAccessTokenError)
nodes.rationale: Sessions looked valid after expiry while Django returned 401 silently; the JWT callback now refreshes and every auth guard checks the error.

nodes.label: UUID v4 guard on upload_id (chunk + complete views)
nodes.norm_label: uuid v4 guard on upload_id (chunk + complete views)

nodes.label: Embed proxy token cache capped at 10,000 entries
nodes.norm_label: embed proxy token cache capped at 10,000 entries

nodes.label: B3 — SKU→layout mapping (built Apr 2026, removed 2026-09-04)
nodes.rationale: Never populated. printo.in resolves SKU→layout itself and passes the layout name into POST /api/embed/session; a second mapping was one more thing to drift. Smoke tests assert /api/sku-layouts/ 404s.

nodes.label: B4 — Server-side upload + render (done Apr 21, 2026)
nodes.rationale: Client-side Fabric→PNG rendering timed out, produced blank frames and crashed low-RAM devices on 100-200 photo orders.

nodes.label: ≤20-canvas client-render threshold removed (v1.8)
nodes.rationale: Every Submit/Download goes through executeServerRender and Celery: one unified contract for webhooks, large batches and resumable uploads, at the cost of ~10-20 s extra latency on small jobs.

nodes.label: Chunked upload API (init / chunk / complete, 2 MB, 4 parallel, 50 MB cap)
nodes.norm_label: chunked upload api (init / chunk / complete, 2 mb, 4 parallel, 50 mb cap)

nodes.label: _smart_downscale — 2x pre-shrink before compositing
nodes.rationale: 12 MP photo → 400 px frame drops working pixels from 12 M to ~0.64 M (~95% memory reduction per frame).

nodes.label: order_id via EmbedSession + X-Order-ID header, never in the iframe URL
nodes.norm_label: order_id via embedsession + x-order-id header, never in the iframe url

nodes.label: DEBUG defaults to off
nodes.rationale: A missing env var previously exposed stack traces in prod.

nodes.label: Pillow memory hygiene (with Image.open, close, del, gc.collect)
nodes.rationale: _generate_for_surface kept canvases alive across iterations; 200-canvas batches accumulated GBs before recycling.
nodes.norm_label: pillow memory hygiene (with image.open, close, del, gc.collect)

nodes.label: worker_max_tasks_per_child 10 → 50
nodes.rationale: Depends on engine.py cleanup being in place.

nodes.label: django-csp in report-only mode
nodes.rationale: The old SECURE_CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY dict was never read by Django; ships report-only so violations are logged before enforcing (Fabric.js needs unsafe-eval).

nodes.label: Single env-driven MAX_UPLOAD_FILE_SIZE_MB
nodes.rationale: Three different limits (10 MB settings, 50 MB validators, hardcoded 50 MB in init view) collapsed into one source.

nodes.label: PIA outage distinguished from bad credentials
nodes.rationale: authorize() used to swallow all errors as 'Invalid credentials'; now 4xx → null, 5xx → PiaServiceUnavailableError, timeout → PiaTimeoutError with 10 s AbortSignal.
nodes.norm_label: pia outage distinguished from bad credentials

nodes.label: src/proxy.ts server-side auth gate
nodes.rationale: Gates /dashboard/* and /editor/layouts/*; /editor/layout/[name] excluded because it serves both dashboard and embed.

nodes.label: Per-IP login rate limiter (5 / 60 s, in-memory)
nodes.rationale: Single-process; must move to Redis before horizontal scale-out.
nodes.norm_label: per-ip login rate limiter (5 / 60 s, in-memory)

nodes.label: B7 — The remaining gap: printo.in webhook consumer
nodes.rationale: Every B1-B6 gap is closed; print files are generated, signed and offered, and nothing collects them, so the manual handoff this PRD exists to delete is still in the loop. The gap is not in this codebase.
nodes.norm_label: b7 — the remaining gap: printo.in webhook consumer

nodes.label: Production readiness sign-off (Mohan)
nodes.rationale: Rollout cannot be scheduled without a fallback path for a print-quality issue preflight would have caught.

nodes.label: Phased rollout (top 5 SKUs → direct-to-production → full catalogue)
nodes.rationale: Keep the preflight team as a spot-check safety net initially.
nodes.norm_label: phased rollout (top 5 skus → direct-to-production → full catalogue)

nodes.label: Arm the orphan-export sweep (GC_ORPHAN_SWEEP dry_run → delete)
nodes.rationale: Disarmed by default because it is the one sweep that deletes on the absence of evidence.
nodes.norm_label: arm the orphan-export sweep (gc_orphan_sweep dry_run → delete)

nodes.label: Sweep expired EmbedSession rows
nodes.rationale: No GC pass deletes them after the 2 h expiry; order-linked rows grow unbounded.

nodes.label: API surface separation (shared render-submission service)
nodes.rationale: Remove the unreachable sync helper in GenerateLayoutView and route both submission paths through one service.

nodes.label: v1.8 — CMYK / soft-proof / ICC pipeline removed; PNG or PDF only
nodes.norm_label: v1.8 — cmyk / soft-proof / icc pipeline removed; png or pdf only

nodes.label: v1.9 — Traefik → nginx 1.27 edge proxy
nodes.rationale: The Traefik acme.json bind-mount footgun produced prod 404s; nginx.conf is single-source with a Cloudflare Origin Cert workflow.

nodes.label: v1.10 — drag clipPath fix, cover white-space clamp, Redis DB split, log rotation, SW
nodes.norm_label: v1.10 — drag clippath fix, cover white-space clamp, redis db split, log rotation, sw

nodes.label: v1.11 — server-side auto-orientation (MediaPipe Pose)
nodes.rationale: Photos stored sideways in the bytes defeat the aspect heuristic; BlazePose derives the body-up vector and snaps to a cardinal with a 30° dead-zone. Mode via AUTO_ORIENTATION_MODE.

nodes.label: v1.12 — server-side overlay rendering
nodes.rationale: Until then every text/shape/image overlay was preview-only: visible in the thumbnail, silently absent from the print. Foundation for the calendar and a fix with far wider reach.

nodes.label: API audit trail (migration 0014, APIRequestLoggingMiddleware)
nodes.rationale: APIRequest existed since the initial commit with nothing writing to it, so count()==0 read as proof a key was never used. api_key became SET_NULL so history survives rotation; 90-day retention outlives the data it describes.

nodes.label: GC staleness + live disk block on /api/celery/monitor/
nodes.rationale: You cannot infer 'did the GC run?' from the DB — tombstones are hard-deleted in the same pass. gc_last_run.json is bind-mounted so it survives recreation; disk is read at request time because the sweep's copy is stale exactly when nothing is sweeping.
nodes.norm_label: gc staleness + live disk block on /api/celery/monitor/

nodes.label: Ops privilege model change (PR #24)
nodes.rationale: Django's IsOpsTeam cannot substitute for a proxy gate because everything through the internal proxy arrives as the one ops-flagged INTERNAL_API_KEY service account; the DPDP purge was re-gated in route.ts by path shape.

nodes.label: Redis DB split (cache db 1, broker db 0)
nodes.rationale: allkeys-lru eviction on a shared db could drop in-flight Celery messages under cache pressure.
nodes.norm_label: redis db split (cache db 1, broker db 0)

nodes.label: pe:render_job postMessage (UX only)
nodes.rationale: Scope narrowed: file delivery is the webhook's job; the storefront frontend does not need to poll.

nodes.label: PRD — Calendar Feature for Product Editor (shipped v1.12/v1.13)
nodes.rationale: Historical design record retained for the why; where it and the code disagree the code is right. Two things shipped differently: a flat ISO-date cell map and a 12-month photo cap.
nodes.norm_label: prd — calendar feature for product editor (shipped v1.12/v1.13)

nodes.label: Per-day entries as one flat { iso_date: [CellOverride] } map
nodes.rationale: Shipped instead of the 12-slot cellsPerCanvas array: entries anchor to globally-unique ISO dates so photo-canvas count changes and English↔Financial flips can never lose or misplace them. Legacy 12-slot arrays are still read on restore.
nodes.norm_label: per-day entries as one flat { iso_date: [celloverride] } map

nodes.label: Photo → month mapping capped at 12 (month i uses photo canvas i mod N)
nodes.rationale: 1 photo cycles to all 12 months, 12 map one-per-month; upload order matters. An earlier build emitted 12·N files in the ZIP.
nodes.norm_label: photo → month mapping capped at 12 (month i uses photo canvas i mod n)

nodes.label: Calendar primitive — a layout-agnostic positioned region
nodes.rationale: Defined by {x,y,width,height} percentages; owns only the grid, cells, pills, holidays and per-cell editing so desk, full-page, poster and side-by-side products come free via layout authoring.
nodes.norm_label: calendar primitive — a layout-agnostic positioned region

nodes.label: Server renderer drew no overlays (pre-v1.12 gap)
nodes.rationale: engine.py had zero ImageDraw/ImageFont imports; text/shape/image overlays were preview-only and vanished from the print. A hard prerequisite for the calendar and valuable on its own.
nodes.norm_label: server renderer drew no overlays (pre-v1.12 gap)

nodes.label: Design principle — minimal customer-facing controls ('templates, not configurators')
nodes.rationale: Every knob is a chance to produce output the design team would not ship; fewer controls cost less to maintain, produce fewer support tickets and protect print quality. Customers wanting more pick a different layout.
nodes.norm_label: design principle — minimal customer-facing controls ('templates, not configurators')

nodes.label: Layout-authored, customer-overridden two-layer model
nodes.rationale: Template (position/size/style) in layout JSON owned by ops; overrides (year, month, cells) in CanvasData.editor_state owned by the customer.

nodes.label: CalendarCellOverride (text | image | hide)
nodes.rationale: Text entries are text-only; dot colour rotates through a 3-slot per-theme cycle by entry index so multi-entry cells stay distinguishable without a picker.

nodes.label: Cells keyed by ISO date, no cell IDs
nodes.rationale: Month change re-derives the cell set automatically; overrides for dates not in the new month stay in the JSON in case the customer flips back.
nodes.norm_label: cells keyed by iso date, no cell ids

nodes.label: Month-grid algorithm (identical client + server math)
nodes.rationale: firstCellOffset = (firstDay - weekStart + 7) % 7; totalCells = ceil((offset + daysInMonth)/7) × 7 → 28/35/42; cellW = usableWidth/7.

nodes.label: Z-order tower — calendar above overlays, below mask
nodes.rationale: calendarZ = overlayZStart + overlays.length + 1 so the calendar is always on top of artwork and the layout mask still wins.
nodes.norm_label: z-order tower — calendar above overlays, below mask

nodes.label: date-fns for month-grid date math
nodes.rationale: ~6 KB tree-shaken; saves ~30 LOC and gives Intl-aware weekday names.

nodes.label: Auto-fit text via ImageFont.getbbox() binary search
nodes.rationale: No library fits either side: DOM auto-fit libs cannot see a <canvas>, and Pillow has no auto-fit — the documented community pattern is ~15 LOC.
nodes.norm_label: auto-fit text via imagefont.getbbox() binary search

nodes.label: Cell images reuse smartcrop + cover-fit + auto-orientation
nodes.rationale: Each cell is a tiny frameSpec, so calculateSmartCropOffsets and _composite_canvas cover math plus the v1.11 MediaPipe pipeline apply with zero new logic.
nodes.norm_label: cell images reuse smartcrop + cover-fit + auto-orientation

nodes.label: Reuse-vs-build cheat-sheet
nodes.rationale: Pure reuse: chunked upload, UploadedFile + GC, IDB persistence, auto-orientation, smartcrop, debouncedRender, fonts endpoint, editor_state, LayoutManagementView, z-order tower, cache invalidation, embed token resolution.

nodes.label: services/overlay_renderer.py — render_overlays()
nodes.rationale: Draws text/shape/image overlays via Pillow ImageDraw after frame compositing and before the paper mask.

nodes.label: services/calendar_renderer.py — render_calendar()
nodes.rationale: Called after render_overlays so the calendar is always on top, matching client z-order.

nodes.label: CalendarEditPanel.tsx — per-cell customer editor
nodes.rationale: Bottom-sheet on narrow viewports because 42 tiny tap targets on a phone is painful.

nodes.label: api/validators.py calendar-block validation
nodes.rationale: Range checks on positions, monthRange.count × calendars.length === 12, banned fields in surfaceOverrides.

nodes.label: TS↔Python grid parity tests (shared fixtures)
nodes.rationale: Any drift between lib/calendar.ts and services/calendar_renderer.py fails CI; both sides consume the same ground truth.

nodes.label: Phase 1 — Server-side overlay rendering (v1.12, ~4 d)
nodes.rationale: The unblocker for everything; ships on its own.

nodes.label: Phase 2 — Calendar product type schema (~3 d)
nodes.norm_label: phase 2 — calendar product type schema (~3 d)

nodes.label: Phase 3 — Style presets + holiday data (~1.5 d)
nodes.norm_label: phase 3 — style presets + holiday data (~1.5 d)

nodes.label: Phase 4 — Calendar renderer client + server (~5 d)
nodes.norm_label: phase 4 — calendar renderer client + server (~5 d)

nodes.label: Risk — Pillow text rendering quality vs browser hinting
nodes.rationale: Mitigation: side-by-side diff in Phase 1; stick to Inter as the safe default.
nodes.norm_label: risk — pillow text rendering quality vs browser hinting

nodes.label: Risk — i18n scope creep
nodes.rationale: Lock v1 to weekStart monday|sunday, Intl weekday names, holidays for en-IN and generic only.

nodes.label: Pill-style cell entries (date always visible, entries stack below)
nodes.norm_label: pill-style cell entries (date always visible, entries stack below)

nodes.label: 3-slot dotCycle per theme / palette
nodes.rationale: Pill background is one theme-wide colour; the dot rotates by entry index so 1st/2nd/3rd entries are distinct without exposing a colour picker.

nodes.label: Global holiday auto-load (holidaySource)
nodes.rationale: Frontend fetches holidays for (locale, year) and injects source:'holiday' entries; the customer cannot delete them but can override the cell with an image.

nodes.label: Three style presets (JSON in storage/calendar_styles/)
nodes.rationale: Ops picks one when authoring; the preset's style block is copied into the layout JSON and can be fine-tuned.

nodes.label: modern-genz preset (4 coordinated palettes)
nodes.rationale: Each palette sets all 6 colour roles together plus a dotCycle; the swatch is the only Gen-Z customer control. New palettes ship as JSON files with no code change.

nodes.label: weekday-highlight preset (Sunday stands out)
nodes.rationale: Single visual cue — light-red fill + red date; no border because it read as a state indicator in review.

nodes.label: Gen-Z palettes (Butter & Purple, Mint & Hot Pink, Lilac & Coral, Sky & Lemon)
nodes.norm_label: gen-z palettes (butter & purple, mint & hot pink, lilac & coral, sky & lemon)

nodes.label: Zero new DB migrations
nodes.rationale: All new data is JSON-shape in existing free-form columns (layout JSON, editor_state); old states deserialise cleanly with the field absent.

nodes.label: productType: 'calendar' — a Multi-Surface Product with a flag
nodes.rationale: Not a separate category (would fork render/ops/preview pipelines) and not pure multi-surface (ops would hand-build 12 surfaces and keep global controls in sync). The flag lets the system auto-generate 12 surfaces from one template with no changes to render, embed or webhook code.
nodes.norm_label: producttype: 'calendar' — a multi-surface product with a flag

nodes.label: Single-template authoring + 12-surface auto-generation
nodes.rationale: Ops designs ONE representative month; the system materializes 12 surfaces at mount / render.

nodes.label: Surface index → (year, month) resolution formula
nodes.rationale: totalOffset = surfaceIndex + (monthOffset ?? 0); realMonth = ((startMonth-1+totalOffset) % 12)+1; realYear = baseYear + floor((startMonth-1+totalOffset)/12).

nodes.label: surfaceOverrides — sparse per-month structural overrides
nodes.rationale: Field-level replace, not deep merge: merging arrays is ambiguous (by id? concatenate? positional?) and each interpretation leaks into UX. Untouched fields inherit from the template; only the diff is persisted.

nodes.label: Ops vs customer control split (§10.3)
nodes.rationale: Aspect ratio and week start ops-locked; theme preset, Gen-Z palette and calendar type customer-changeable; year auto-populated.

nodes.label: defaultYear: 'current' — auto-rolling year
nodes.rationale: Layout files never freeze to a year; a layout published in 2026 prints 2027 dates from Jan 1, 2027 with zero ops intervention.

nodes.label: Calendar type — English (Jan..Dec) vs Financial (Apr..Mar)
nodes.rationale: Same SKU; baseYear = today.month >= Apr ? year : year-1 for financial. Drives startMonth so it must stay layout-global.

nodes.label: Photobook as the next productType
nodes.rationale: Reuses multi-surface render, single-template authoring, embed/ZIP/webhook; differs in variable N, no calendar primitive, spreads.

nodes.label: productType is the extension point for new products
nodes.rationale: Each productType gets its own ops and preview UIs but shares the storage + render layer.
nodes.norm_label: producttype is the extension point for new products

nodes.label: Multi-calendar single-surface (year-on-one-poster) mode
nodes.rationale: monthRange.count = 1, calendars.length = 12, each with explicit monthOffset.

nodes.label: Constraint: monthRange.count × calendars.length === 12
nodes.rationale: Validator rejects other products; mixed grids are mathematically valid but the UI ships only the two patterns.

nodes.label: Cell-image expiry — 'Image expired, please re-upload'
nodes.rationale: Follows the UploadedFile GC policy; no automatic recovery because embed sessions are short-lived enough that this is rare.

nodes.label: Calendar type flip warning modal (orphaned entries hidden, not deleted)
nodes.norm_label: calendar type flip warning modal (orphaned entries hidden, not deleted)

nodes.label: Multi-surface partial failure — fail-all-or-nothing
nodes.rationale: If any 1 of N surfaces fails the whole RenderJob fails and retry re-renders all N; per-surface retry is v2.

nodes.label: ZIP filenames from displayLabel ('January 2026.png')
nodes.rationale: Financial-year calendars span 'April 2026.png … March 2027.png'; non-calendar multi-surface products use the ops-set label.

nodes.label: §11.7 — Single bundled font (Inter Variable), no picker
nodes.rationale: Removes fontFamily/fontWeight from the schema: no font drift between preview and 300 DPI render, simpler authoring, and the 'font missing' failure mode is eliminated.
nodes.norm_label: §11.7 — single bundled font (inter variable), no picker

nodes.label: Feb 29 entries on non-leap years — one-time toast, entries kept
nodes.norm_label: feb 29 entries on non-leap years — one-time toast, entries kept

nodes.label: scripts/refresh-holidays.py — annual ops task
nodes.rationale: A year without a holiday file renders with no auto-injection rather than an error.

nodes.label: Hard cap of 3 entries per cell, no '+N more'
nodes.norm_label: hard cap of 3 entries per cell, no '+n more'

nodes.label: MAX_ENTRIES precedence — user-first
nodes.rationale: Reverses the original holidays-first rule: customer intent beats auto-injection; a suppressed holiday reappears when a user entry is removed.

nodes.label: Out-of-month filler cells — date number only
nodes.rationale: No entries, pills or images: cleaner and avoids 'is this entry for this month or the next?' ambiguity.
nodes.norm_label: out-of-month filler cells — date number only

nodes.label: IST-only, ISO date strings end-to-end
nodes.rationale: The renderer never calls datetime.now(); the frontend computes 'today' in Asia/Kolkata. All v1 customers are in India.

nodes.label: Validator rejects banned fields in surfaceOverrides
nodes.rationale: themePreset, calendarType, weekStart, canvas, monthRange are layout-global; banning them stops ops bypassing the rule via manual JSON edits.
nodes.norm_label: validator rejects banned fields in surfaceoverrides

nodes.label: No layout versioning — fresh load on every embed
nodes.rationale: Acceptable for v1 because sessions are short-lived and ops rarely edits published layouts mid-quarter; add layoutVersion if edit frequency rises.
nodes.norm_label: no layout versioning — fresh load on every embed

nodes.label: v2 readiness — signed S3 download URL
nodes.rationale: The Next.js proxy buffers full ZIPs (~300 MB peak); v1 keeps download_url, RenderJobDownloadView and the output path S3-friendly so v2 is a contained swap.
nodes.norm_label: v2 readiness — signed s3 download url

nodes.label: Reuse of storage/fonts.json + FontsView (original proposal)
nodes.rationale: Superseded by §11.7's single bundled font.

nodes.label: Printo Wordmark: orange lowercase 'printo' with registered mark, tagline 'easy, one-stop printing', purple circle emblem at left
nodes.norm_label: printo wordmark: orange lowercase 'printo' with registered mark, tagline 'easy, one-stop printing', purple circle emblem at left

nodes.label: Printo Brand Colours: deep purple emblem (~#64318E) + orange wordmark (~#F17A26)
nodes.norm_label: printo brand colours: deep purple emblem (~#64318e) + orange wordmark (~#f17a26)

nodes.label: Tailwind indigo scale overridden to Printo purple #64318E; accent orange #F17A26 as literal hex
nodes.norm_label: tailwind indigo scale overridden to printo purple #64318e; accent orange #f17a26 as literal hex

hyperedges.label: Embed session → proxy header injection → render → signed webhook
Signed webhook delivery contract (payload, HMAC, ZIP fetch, retries)
Calendar product type: template → 12 surfaces → render → labelled ZIP
Celery task safety rules (retry discipline, dispatch, poison-pill, webhook isolation)
